title: runtime: add debug endpoint/CLI to explain kernel selection decisions
author: Omar El-Sayed
body:
## Summary
Adds an operator/debug-only way to answer: “why did the runtime pick *this* kernel for *this* request context?”. This is primarily for Kernel auto-selection v2 rollout debugging and perf investigations.

This PR introduces:
- **HTTP debug endpoint** (disabled by default) that returns a structured explanation of the selection path and inputs used.
- **CLI wrapper** that can either (a) query a running runtime via the debug endpoint, or (b) run the selector locally with a provided context payload.

This is intended to unblock oncall + perf work during staged rollout where we need fast root cause for regressions (e.g., wrong seq bucket or unexpected GPU normalization).

## Motivation
During canaries we frequently need to confirm:
- Which selector version (v1 vs v2) was used
- Model family detection result + any fallback
- GPU SKU normalization output (esp. MIG/partitioned environments)
- Effective seq-length bucket / phase (prefill vs decode)
- Which registry entry matched, and why other candidates were rejected

Today the only way is digging through traces/metrics or reproducing locally with ad-hoc printf. This PR adds a deterministic “explain” path with consistent formatting.

## Design
### Endpoint
- New endpoint: `GET /internal/debug/kernel-selection/explain`
- Only registered when `runtime.debug_endpoints_enabled=true`
- Requires auth: either (a) operator mTLS identity with `runtime.debug` scope, or (b) `X-Redwood-Debug-Token` configured on the node (intended for air-gapped/Private installs). Hosted control plane will keep `runtime.debug_endpoints_enabled=false`.
- Accepts a JSON payload describing the selection context (model id + metadata overrides, gpu info overrides, seq lengths/phase). Returns a JSON explanation.

### CLI
Adds `redwood-runtime debug explain-kernel-choice`:
- `--endpoint https://…` to query a running cluster (requires debug token)
- or `--context-file /path/to/context.json` to run locally

### Output schema (high-level)
The response is designed to be copy/paste-able into Slack and also machine-parsable.
Fields include:
- `selector_version_used`: v2|v1
- `inputs`: model_family, gqa flag, head_dim, dtype, quant_profile, phase, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_normalized, sm, etc.
- `decision_trace`: ordered steps (registry load -> family match -> gpu match -> seq bucket match -> candidate filter -> tie-break)
- `final_choice`: kernel_id + kernel impl + “safe set” membership
- `fallbacks`: if any

Example (truncated):
{
  "selector_version_used": "v2",
  "inputs": {"model_family":"mistral-family","phase":"decode","seq_bucket":"ctx_4k_8k","gpu":"A10"},
  "decision_trace": [
    "registry=v1.3.0 loaded (216 entries)",
    "matched rule: mistral-family/decode/ctx_4k_8k/gpu=A10 -> kernel=attn.flash_v3_decode_sm80",
    "tie-break: highest priority entry (priority=90)"
  ],
  "final_choice": {"kernel_id":"attn.flash_v3_decode_sm80","why":"highest priority exact match"},
  "fallbacks": []
}

## Implementation notes
- Added `ExplainSelection()` alongside the normal selection path; it shares the same internal codepath and simply records the intermediate decisions.
- Explanation recording is gated and does not run on hot path. Selector hot path remains unchanged.
- We explicitly avoid emitting full model metadata or request payload. Only fields already present in selection context are surfaced.
- Added redaction for any unknown/extra metadata keys passed via overrides.

## Testing
- Unit tests for deterministic decision trace ordering.
- Tests for auth gating (endpoint unavailable when disabled; 403 without scope/token).
- Golden tests for a few canonical contexts (llama-family prefill, mistral decode long, unknown model family fallback).

## Rollout
- No behavior change by default (debug endpoints disabled).
- For internal perf lab + Dedicated eval clusters, enable via config and use debug token.

## Checklist
- [x] Endpoint is internal-only + gated by config
- [x] AuthZ enforced (scope/token)
- [x] Output schema documented in `docs/runtime/debugging.md`
- [x] Does not add new high-cardinality metrics

Related: ENG-3932 (debug tool), ENG-3927 (telemetry), ENG-3923 (selector v2 core)

Screenshots/logs: n/a (text output only)
commits: tests: golden traces + auth gating coverage
docs: debugging guide for kernel selection explain output
review_conversation: Grace Kim (review): The trace output is great. Two asks: (1) ensure tie-break reasoning is explicit when multiple candidates match; (2) please include seq bucket boundaries in the output so we can spot off-by-one issues quickly.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Added explicit `tie_break` field + appended bucket boundary string (e.g. ctx_4k_8k => [4096, 8192)). Also added a unit test where two candidates match and priority wins.
Yuki Sato (review): For GPU normalization, can we include both raw + normalized SKU and SM capability? This will help with MIG partitions where nvidia-smi reports differently.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Done. `inputs.gpu_raw` + `inputs.gpu_normalized` + `inputs.sm` now included. For MIG, we also include `partition` when available.

Allison Grant (review): Please confirm this won’t ship enabled for Hosted. Also, make sure we don’t accidentally add new metrics labels or log spam. The endpoint output should not be emitted into logs by default.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Confirmed: endpoint is only registered when `runtime.debug_endpoints_enabled=true` (default false in all Hosted configs). No metrics added. No logging of response payload; only request count and status at debug level (and that is sampled).

Benji Okafor (security review): Token-based auth is fine for Private, but please ensure token is never accepted over non-TLS unless explicitly configured. Also, scope-based auth should be preferred when mTLS identity exists.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated: token auth requires TLS unless `runtime.allow_insecure_debug_token=true` (default false; intended only for local dev). Also reordered auth: mTLS scope checked first, token fallback second. Added tests.
Grace Kim (approval): LGTM after last push. This will save us a lot of time during canary investigations.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping it config-gated + low risk.
merge_commit: 9b7c2df (squash): add debug explain endpoint for kernel selector decisions
release_notes: Adds an internal, config-gated debug endpoint and CLI command to explain kernel selection decisions (selector version, inputs, matched registry rule, fallbacks). No behavior change by default.
